clue.text: Aid to driver's prospect, we'll engage one cracking whips

indicators.note: to engage is to take in or hold, so the first word holds the rest within it
cracking means breaking apart, so the word whips is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the pronoun we, taken as written, as the outer shell
one is the article A
the letters of whips, rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach driver's warning that someone will step in to stop a whip-cracking scene.
explanation.walkthrough: WE (the 'we' of we'll) holds A plus a jumble of WHIPS: W(A SHWIP)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash-wipe is the windscreen washer and wiper system that keeps a motorist's forward view clear.

clue.text: Doings at Davos? Tense porter's employed with gains around (12, two words)

indicators.note: around means the word for gains wraps about the jumbled letters
employed suggests letters being put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: first part of WINS, gains, which is split to hold the rest
T for tense plus the letters of porter's, rearranged
last letter of WINS closes the shell

explanation.surface: A tense hotel porter is hired on good pay at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: T (tense, grammar abbreviation) joins PORTERS in the anagram, all inside WINS. Davos is a Swiss ski resort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing, bobsleigh and similar activities are what visitors to the Alpine resort do, an example-style definition.

clue.text: Dog, one breed that's trained with measure of dash

an en is a printer's measure, the width of an en dash

explanation.surface: A dog of one breed is trained to show some dash.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdeen terrier is another name for the Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Instrument for chopping a slate suitable for one's rockery

taken as written
a slate is a kind of roofing tile

explanation.surface: A tool for cutting slate is recommended for building a garden rockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music and the saxophone, but here SAX is the slater's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxatile describes plants and creatures living among rocks, which suits the stony setting of a rock garden.

clue.text: Last of a casserole used as starter — to avoid this?

definitions.text: Last of a casserole used as starter — to avoid this?

parts.note: a stew is a casserole

explanation.walkthrough: Move the last letter of A STEW to the front to get WASTE; read whole, the clue describes thriftily serving up leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving up leftovers is a way to avoid throwing food away, which is the squandering the answer names.

clue.text: Producer of ferrous sulphate modified skin shade

a shade or tint of colour

explanation.surface: A chemical compound causes a change in skin colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkstone is a mineral containing iron sulphate, once used in making ink, so it is a source of the salt.

clue.text: Some real barren mounts, bleak in the Cairngorms?

explanation.walkthrough: The Cairngorms are Scottish mountains, flagging a Scots word: blae means bleak or livid blue-grey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means livid or bleak and sunless, so it suits the Highland setting.

clue.text: Expectant woman's affliction? Reduced energy immobilizes end of pregnancy

clue.text: Signifying 'doer', one brought in untangled a tangle

the Roman numeral
